items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: MR: Greetings. My name is Monk Rowe of the Hamilton College Music Department. We are filming for our jazz archive today and as a very special event, we have two of the jazz greats with us this afternoon, Mr. Milt Hinton, bassist extraordinaire, and the great jazz vocalist Joe Williams.

ctx.x: Milt was interviewed by jazz vocalist and friend Joe Williams on May 31, 1995 aboard a cruise ship in the Caribbean.

MR: Greetings. My name is Monk Rowe of the Hamilton College Music Department. We are filming for our jazz archive today and as a very special event, we have two of the jazz greats with us this afternoon, Mr. Milt Hinton, bassist extraordinaire, and the great jazz vocalist Joe Williams. And we’re going to let them talk, and relate some of their experiences in the world of jazz.

Yeah. I keep my eye on the ladies, you know. My first one she was a real lady. She was a doll. And as I say this woman, it was either her or the one with the one eye. What was the one that had the one eye? What was her name, Hop? Anyhow, so she walked over the stage, you know, went down, the show was over, the Club DeLisa you know, so here comes the strolling singer and this woman. And she walked up to him and she started right away. [sings] I’m going to lock my car and throw away the key, I’m tired of you…
